newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ECUADOR COACH MATURANA SAYS FUTURE UNCERTAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ECUADOR COACH MATURANA SAYS FUTURE UNCERTAIN.

text.p: Ecuador coach Francisco Maturana said on Thursday he may leave the job as soon as the World Cup qualifying matches finish in November.

"I'm comfortable in Ecuador but my contract finishes after the (World Cup qualifying) game against Uruguay and we have't yet spoken about renewing it," he said, adding that "personal expectations" could persuade him to step down.
Maturana, who led his own country Colombia out of the soccer wilderness to two consecutive World Cups, is now trying to get Ecuador to the finals for the first time in their history.
Paraguay, Argentina and Colombia appear set to take three of South America's four qualifying places and Ecuador are fighting Bolivia, Uruguay, Peru and Chile in a tight battle for the last.

Maturana is making only a brief visit to Bolivia. Ecuador has rested its top players instead of bringing them to compete for the Copa, which has been crammed between World Cup qualifiers, and the team is being led by his assistant Luis Fernando Suarez.
Ecuador drew 0-0 with Argentina, who also had their top players missing, in their opening game on Wednesday.
